slides.texte_overlay:
hobbies that will make you
intellectually lethal

steelmanning

once a week, write the strongest possible version of an argument you disagree with. understanding the other side properly makes your own thinking very hard to beat.

reading primary sources

read the original speech, letter or study instead of the article about it. going to the source is slower, but you'll catch what every summary left out.

chess endgames

study one chess endgame a week. thinking a few moves ahead in a game trains the same calm, careful logic you'll use in every serious decision of your life.

one idea a day

spend 5 minutes a day learning one big idea: a theory, a famous experiment, a turning point in history. sharp minds are built from many small doses, not one big push.
slides.texte_sophia:
one idea a day

i used to read only headlines. now i spend 5 minutes a day on one lesson in the Sophia app: a theory, an experiment, a turning point in history. sharp minds are built daily.

slides.texte_overlay:
explaining to a child

explain one hard thing a week as if to a ten year old. if you can't make it simple, you've found exactly the part you still need to go back and understand.
